items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request force-pushes to the existing branch rather than opening a duplicate pull request. The diff delivers what it says — `update_reviewable`, `update_change` on both GitHub and GitLab adapters, `fetch_branch` on `GitLocal`, the person-commit and unreadable-branch refusals, the `mark_draft` inverse, and a substantial test file covering all thirteen named discharge tests. The design documentation and obje…[truncated]
GitLab `update_change` commits with `title_line(subject)` but GitHub commits with `subject` directly.

`_existing_change_for` falls through to open-new on `changes_for` error, but the description says the gate holds both directions separately — the test for this path exists, but the asymmetry with `_branch_state` is documented only in a comment.

This change adds an update path for a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request: instead of opening a new pull request it fetches the existing branch, checks for person-authored commits, and force-pushes with a lease. The performance lens looks for queries inside loops, unbounded reads, and work that scales with usage. This change adds a second-`/implement`-updates-existing-PR path, with force-push leased on a freshly-fetched sha, person-commit detection via trailer inspection, and a `mark_draft` inverse. The security-relevant controls are the lease preventing a blind overwrite, the credential-stripping of git stderr before public posting, and the `assert_run_scoped` check that gates both `update_change` implementations. I reviewed both adapter implementations and the orchestrating `implement_propose` path. Th…[truncated]
`assert_run_scoped` is called on a branch that was opened by a different run, and its check may be weaker than documented here.
An error from `changes_for` silently falls back to opening a new PR, and the asymmetry with the unreadable-branch refusal is undocumented at the call site.
